title: Naruto and Sasuke to Fight Again in Kishimoto's Naruto: Shadow Rising | Entertainment
text:
Naruto and Sasuke will fight again in Naruto: Shadow Rising, Masashi Kishimoto's new manga set in the Blank Period after the Fourth Great Ninja War.
Naruto and Sasuke will fight again in Naruto: Shadow Rising, the new manga illustrated by series creator Masashi Kishimoto, set during the long-awaited Blank Period after the Fourth Great Ninja War. Early glimpses of Kishimoto's return show what appears to be a two-page spread depicting a clash between the two rivals, though little else has been revealed about the encounter.
Naruto and Sasuke rivalry history
The rivalry between Naruto and Sasuke is among the few in anime and manga that matches conflicting ideologies, isolating trauma and dramatic reconciliation. Their fights have ranged from lop-sided jealousy to catalysts for mutual growth, with moments that could almost be mistaken for romantic undercurrents.
When they fight, in either the manga or the anime, their clashes grew more explosive with their development as shinobi. These encounters moved from school-set sparring matches to embittered hospital rooftop jutsu-measuring, to meetings after the Five Kage Summit and twice at the Valley of the End.
Moments like these should be carefully relished, much like Dragon Ball fans flocking to the next bout between Goku and Vegeta. The upcoming clash is expected to be unique for more ways than one.
The headband promise from chapter 699
Naruto and Sasuke settled their differences after stopping Kaguya and ending the Fourth Great Ninja War, allowing them to move forward with their lives. Upon Sasuke's release from prison, he went on a journey abroad to atone for his sins.
Before he departed, Naruto gave him one last gift: his Konoha headband, the same one he had defaced in their first fight at the Valley of the End. Sasuke accepted it, saying he would hang onto it until they had their real fight, as depicted in Naruto chapter 699.
That moment marked the start of Sasuke's new life as what would eventually become Konoha's Supporting Kage. His bond with Naruto became one of mutual, unspoken trust, having left their grudges and one hand each in the past.
It is easy to dismiss this as a playful tease within a rivalry that will never truly be settled. In another way, it is the perfect setup for another fight, if simply to see how far they have come.
This is significant because, unlike both times at the Valley of the End, Sasuke shows willingness to see Naruto as his equal. There is also the implicit intent not to kill his opponent, after Naruto finally broke through to him and showed him the errors of his ways.
Fighting in their post-war prime
Even more exciting than the fight itself is that this is both a microcosm of what is likely to come with other Naruto: Shadow Rising fights and a unique clash of Naruto and Sasuke in their post-war prime.
Now fully adults and starting families of their own, Naruto and Sasuke have grown older, wiser and more competent with their talents. These include Naruto's bond with Kurama and Sasuke's use of his Rinnegan and Sharingan eyes.
Sasuke may lack the use of one hand, but as seen in Boruto, that never seemed to slow him down. If anything, the Naruto versus Sasuke fight teased in Shadow Rising's glimpses might simply set up a distillation of how far each character has come since the end of the war.
The story is likely to set up the opportunity for them to test each other's limits, akin to Goku and Vegeta training under Whis in Dragon Ball Super. Given how spectacular their team coordination is hinted to be, such as in Boruto: Naruto Next Generations chapter 8, Kishimoto has the chance to set up something similar.
Written and illustrated by Kishimoto himself, the encounter could be the singular most satisfying moment promised so far in Naruto: Shadow Rising, expanding the documented events of the Naruto timeline.
